title: Glutamate clearance at two sites
summary: Ceftriaxone as a conditional astrocyte comparator in WWOX loss of function.

graph.evidence: Total GLT-1 rose without faster decay in healthy slices.
graph.inference: A local signal can shrink through uptake, dispersion or release.
graph.hypothesis: Surface transport may be constrained by sodium recovery.
graph.experiment: Measure both sites after the same calibrated glutamate input.

evidence: In Tsc1 mice, starting before seizure onset reduced recorded frequency. Starting after onset raised GLT-1 with no detected EEG benefit. Human ALS efficacy was unconfirmed.
inference: WWOX bulk SLC1A2 fell. Pooled astrocyte Slc1a2 rose after removing it from cell assignment. Atp1a2 fell in that pool. Measure native transport and ionic reserve.
hypothesis: Improved uptake should reduce near and distal glutamate after a fixed pulse. Faster dispersion can shorten near decay while increasing distal spillover.
experiment: Pair local free exposure, surface EAAT2, sodium recovery and near/distal glutamate with a transporter dependency control. Test first recruitment separately.
limits: Conditional ex vivo comparison. Pediatric CSF data come mainly from infection-related care. Prolonged adult exposure increased hepatobiliary events.
